sentences.text:
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Neeraj Kumar Sharma, learned Aga and perused the
material available on record.

2.  This application has been filed seeking anticipatory bail in Case Crime No. 437 of 2024, under sections 376, 506 IPC and Section 66C of the Information Technology Act, Police Station Ghoorpur,
District- Allahabad.
3. Counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the instant case.
The marriage of the applicant was fixed with the informant-victim.
Subsequently, due to certain reasons, the marriage of the applicant could not be solemnized with the informant.
Subsequently, the instant FIR has been lodged.

sentences.text: has not supported the prosecution version
, she stated that the applicant has not acted indecently with her and she does not want to institute any proceedings against the applicant.
However, the victim in her statement under Section 183 BNSS has supported the prosecution version.
She stated that the applicant established physical relation with her on pretext of marriage and made indecent video.
It is contended that the contradiction in the statement of the victim under Sections 180 BNSS and 183 BNSS discredits the prosecution case.
No indecent video has been collected by the Investigating Officer.
The applicant has no criminal antecedents.

The named co-accused Hari Shankar (father of the applicant) has been granted anticipatory bail by the Addl. Sessions Judge/FTC-2, Prayagraj vide order dated 20.01.2025 passed in Anticipatory Bail Application No.
214 of 2025 (Hari Shankar Vs. State of U.P.).

entities.text: Hari Shankar Vs. State of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is next submitted that the investigation is going on and the applicant has apprehension of his arrest in the above mentioned case.
4. Learned A.G.A. opposed the prayer for anticipatory bail but could not satisfactorily dispute the aforesaid submissions from the record.
5. Learned counsel for the applicant further submits that the application for grant of anticipatory bail be confined only till the submission of the police report.

6. Having regard to the submissions made by learned counsel for the applicant, considering the nature of accusations and antecedents of the applicant, in particular the fact, that there are contradiction in the statement of the victim under Sections 180 BNSS and 183 BNSS, no indecent video of the victim has been collected by the Investigating Officer, the named co-accused Hari Shankar (father of the applicant) has been granted anticipatory bail by the Addl. Sessions Judge/FTC-2, Prayagraj, without commenting on merits of the case, I am of the opinion that the applicant is entitled to be enlarged on anticipatory bail till the submission of police report.
8. In default of any of the conditions, the Investigating Officer is at liberty to file appropriate application for cancellation of anticipatory bail granted to the applicant.
